records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new speech: the offerings of the whole people through the year
decisions.reason: The new generation has been counted (chapter 26) and Joshua has been named to lead them into the land (27:12-23). This speech, which runs to the end of chapter 29, sets out the offerings Israel is to bring for the whole people, day by day, week by week, month by month and at each yearly festival. Moses passes it on to the people in 30:1.

records.heading: The daily offerings

records.source: צַ֚ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אֶת־קָרְבָּנִ֨י לַחְמִ֜י לְאִשַּׁ֗י רֵ֚יחַ נִֽיחֹחִ֔י תִּשְׁמְר֕וּ לְהַקְרִ֥יב לִ֖י בְּמוֹעֲדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Command [the] sons of Israel and say to them, my offering, my food for my offerings by fire, [the] aroma of my soothing, you will take care to present to me at its appointed time.
pieces: "Command the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'Be careful to present to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at its appointed time {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offering, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food, given as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food offerings, a soothing aroma to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.2: "Command the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'My offering, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offerings by fire, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} aroma of soothing, you shall take care to present to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at its appointed time.'

R.2: "Command the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Be sure to bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offerings, each at the time I have set. They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food, food offerings burned on the altar, and their smell pleases {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: my food: the offerings pictured as a meal at God's table
decisions.reason: The offerings are called God's food, as in Leviticus 3:11 and 21:6, a picture of gifts set before a king at his table. It does not mean that God needs to be fed: Psalm 50:12-13 says plainly that he does not. The picture shows that these gifts belong to him and are received by him.

decisions.choice: my offerings by fire, my aroma of soothing: gifts burned on the altar that God gladly accepts
decisions.reason: For the offering by fire see 15:3: a gift burned, wholly or in part, on the altar. The smoke is pictured as a smell that calms and pleases God, so that he accepts the people who bring it (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9).

decisions.choice: you shall take care ... at its appointed time: each offering on its fixed day, a duty of the whole people
decisions.reason: "You" is plural: the whole people are responsible that the offerings are never left off or brought at the wrong time. "Its appointed time" uses the word for the festivals (Leviticus 23:2, 4). Leviticus 23 gave the dates of the festivals; chapters 28-29 give the offerings for each of them (Leviticus 23:37).

decisions.choice: food offerings
decisions.reason: As in 15:3, Balanced and Readable say "food offering", and Readable adds "burned on the altar". Literal keeps "offerings by fire". Balanced keeps "food" and "food offerings" side by side, as the Hebrew puts them.

decisions.choice: Be careful to present ... / Be sure to bring ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the offerings first and puts the command at the end. Balanced and Readable put the command first, so that the sentence is easy to follow. Readable makes the description of the offerings a sentence of its own.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם זֶ֚ה הָֽאִשֶּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ לַיהוָ֑ה כְּבָשִׂ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֧ה תְמִימִ֛ם שְׁנַ֥יִם לַיּ֖וֹם עֹלָ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And you will say to them, this [is] the offering by fire which you will present to Yahweh: lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, two for the day, [a] burnt offering continually.
pieces: Tell them: 'Each day you are to present to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as a food offering, two year-old male lambs without defect. This is the regular burnt offering.

L.3: And you shall say to them, 'This [is] the offering by fire which you shall present to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: male lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, two each day, a continual burnt offering.

R.3: Tell them: 'Here is the food offering burned on the altar that you must bring to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Every day bring two male lambs one year old, with nothing wrong with them. Offer them as a burnt offering every day without fail.

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, every day without a break
decisions.reason: The word means constant or regular. Used of an offering, it means one that is brought every day and never left off. The daily burnt offering was first commanded in Exodus 29:38-42, and the same word marks it there.

decisions.choice: sons of a year, unblemished: one year old, with no defect
decisions.reason: "Son of a year" means an animal in its first year (Exodus 12:5; Leviticus 23:12). An offering had to be whole and sound, with no injury or flaw (Leviticus 22:19-22).

decisions.choice: and you shall say to them: Moses is to pass on the list that follows
decisions.reason: God now gives Moses the words to say to the people. The list runs from here to the end of chapter 29. The calendar starts with the daily offering, since every other offering in it is added to this one (verses 10, 15, 23, 24, 31).

decisions.choice: regular burnt offering / every day without fail
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "continual". Balanced says "regular", as in Exodus 29:42. Readable says what the word means: an offering brought every day without fail.

records.source: אֶת־הַכֶּ֥בֶשׂ אֶחָ֖ד תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַבֹּ֑קֶר וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָֽעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: The lamb, one, you will offer in the morning, and the lamb, the second, you will offer between the evenings.
pieces: One lamb is to be offered in the morning, and the other as evening comes on.

L.4: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer between the two evenings.

R.4: Offer one of them in the morning and one in the evening.

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at dusk, as day turns into night
decisions.reason: The same phrase sets the time of the evening lamb in Exodus 29:39 and of the Passover in Leviticus 23:5 and Numbers 9:3. It means the time when evening comes on. Its exact span is not settled; see Leviticus 23:5.

decisions.choice: you shall offer: the command now speaks to Israel as one
decisions.reason: The verbs change from "you" plural (verse 3) to "you" singular. The same people are meant, now addressed as one body, as often in these laws (15:5).

decisions.choice: as evening comes on / in the evening
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 23:5, Balanced says "as evening comes on" and Readable "in the evening". Literal keeps "between the two evenings".

records.source: וַעֲשִׂירִ֧ית הָאֵיפָ֛ה סֹ֖לֶת לְמִנְחָ֑ה בְּלוּלָ֛ה בְּשֶׁ֥מֶן כָּתִ֖ית רְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִֽין׃
records.gloss: And [a] tenth of the ephah [of] fine flour for [a] grain offering, mixed with oil, pressed, [a] fourth of the hin.
pieces: The grain offering for each lamb is to be {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of pressed olive oil.

L.5: And a tenth of the ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of the hin of pressed oil.

R.5: With each lamb, bring a grain offering of {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of the best olive oil.

decisions.choice: a tenth of the ephah; a fourth of the hin: about two quarts of flour and a quart of oil
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure of about twenty quarts, so a tenth of it was about two quarts. The hin was a liquid measure of about a gallon, so a quarter of it was about a quart. These are the amounts for a lamb in Exodus 29:40 and Numbers 15:4.

decisions.choice: pressed oil: the finest olive oil
decisions.reason: The word means beaten or crushed. It names oil beaten from olives, which gave the clearest oil, the kind used for the lamp (Exodus 27:20) and for the daily offering (Exodus 29:40).

decisions.choice: for a grain offering: with each of the two lambs
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb; it adds the grain offering to the lamb of verse 4. Verse 7 says "for each lamb", and verse 8 gives the evening lamb the same grain offering as the morning one, so the amounts are for each lamb.

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts; about a quart (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in 15:4, Balanced and Readable give modern measures, with the ancient ones as the alternative wording. Literal keeps "a tenth of the ephah" and "a quarter of the hin". Balanced and Readable say "for each lamb" or "with each lamb" to join the verse to verse 4, and Readable says "the best olive oil" for "pressed oil".

records.source: עֹלַ֖ת תָּמִ֑יד הָעֲשֻׂיָה֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י לְרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: [A] burnt offering of continuity, the [one] made at [the] mountain of Sinai for [an] aroma of soothing, [an] offering by fire to Yahweh.
pieces: It is the regular burnt offering, as it was offered at Mount Sinai: a soothing aroma, a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: [It is] a continual burnt offering, the one made at Mount Sinai, for an aroma of soothing, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: This is the daily burnt offering that was first offered at Mount Sinai. It is a food offering burned on the altar, and its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the one made at Mount Sinai: the daily offering began at Sinai
decisions.reason: The daily offering was commanded at Sinai (Exodus 29:38-42) and began when the priests started their work there (Leviticus 9:17). The new generation is to go on with the same offering their parents brought at the mountain.

decisions.choice: made: offered at Sinai, not only commanded there
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for offering the lambs in verse 4, so it most likely means the offering that was brought at Sinai. It could also mean the offering that was set up or ordained there. The difference is small: either way the daily offering goes back to Sinai.

decisions.choice: [It is]
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb in Hebrew. Literal brackets "It is"; Balanced and Readable say it without brackets. Readable adds "first" to show that the offering began at Sinai and goes on.

records.source: וְנִסְכּוֹ֙ רְבִיעִ֣ת הַהִ֔ין לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד בַּקֹּ֗דֶשׁ הַסֵּ֛ךְ נֶ֥סֶךְ שֵׁכָ֖ר לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And its drink offering [is] [a] fourth of the hin for the lamb, the one; in the holy place pour out [a] drink offering of strong drink to Yahweh.
pieces: Its drink offering is to be {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} for each lamb. In the holy place pour out the drink offering of strong drink to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.7: And its drink offering [shall be] a quarter of the hin for each lamb; in the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: For each lamb, also bring {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} of strong drink as a drink offering. Pour it out for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the holy place.

decisions.choice: strong drink: here, the strong wine of the drink offering
decisions.reason: The word names a fermented drink stronger than ordinary wine, and is often paired with wine (Leviticus 10:9; Numbers 6:3). Elsewhere the drink offering is of wine (15:5; Exodus 29:40), and verse 14 says "wine", so here the word probably means strong wine. It may instead mean that another fermented drink could be used.

decisions.choice: in the holy place: at the altar in the court of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: "The holy place" here means the sanctuary area. The drink offering was not poured on the incense altar inside the tent (Exodus 30:9), so it was poured out at the altar of burnt offering, where the lamb was burned.

decisions.choice: for each lamb: each of the two lambs has its drink offering
decisions.reason: "The one lamb" means each lamb, as in 15:5. For the drink offering see 15:5.

decisions.choice: strong drink
decisions.reason: All three levels keep "strong drink", so that the reader can see that the word differs from the "wine" of verse 14. The meaning decision explains it.

records.source: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָֽעַרְבָּ֑יִם כְּמִנְחַ֨ת הַבֹּ֤קֶר וּכְנִסְכּוֹ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And the lamb, the second, you will offer between the evenings; like [the] grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you will offer, [an] offering by fire, [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh.
pieces: The second lamb you are to offer as evening comes on, with a grain offering and a drink offering like those of the morning: a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: And the second lamb you shall offer between the two evenings; like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you shall offer [it], an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: Offer the other lamb in the evening, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a food offering burned on the altar, and its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: like the grain offering of the morning: the same amounts as verses 5 and 7
decisions.reason: The evening lamb has the same grain offering and drink offering as the morning lamb. For "between the two evenings" see verse 4.

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The daily offering, morning and evening, is a gift the LORD gladly accepts.

records.source: וּבְיוֹם֙ הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת שְׁנֵֽי־כְבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֖ה תְּמִימִ֑ם וּשְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֧לֶת מִנְחָ֛ה בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן וְנִסְכּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And on [the] day of the sabbath two lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, and two tenths [of] fine flour [as a] grain offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering,
pieces: On the Sabbath day there are to be two year-old male lambs without defect, with {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering,

L.9: And on the sabbath day, two male lambs, sons of a year, unblemished, and two tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering,

R.9: On the Sabbath day, offer two male lambs one year old, with nothing wrong with them. With them bring a grain offering of {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with olive oil, and the drink offering that goes with it.

decisions.choice: on the sabbath day: two more lambs, doubling the daily offering
decisions.reason: On the Sabbath, the seventh day of every week (Leviticus 23:3), two lambs are added to the two of the daily offering. The Sabbath is set apart by the offering as well as by rest.

decisions.choice: two tenths ... and its drink offering: one grain offering for the two lambs
decisions.reason: The two tenths of flour, about four quarts, are the grain offering for both lambs together, a tenth for each as in verse 5. The amount of the drink offering is not given; it is probably a quarter of a hin for each lamb, as in verse 7. The verse has no verb, and the sentence ends in verse 10.

decisions.choice: about 4 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Literal brackets "of an ephah", which the Hebrew leaves out. Balanced supplies "there are to be" and Readable "offer", since the verse has no verb.

records.heading: Sabbath offerings

records.source: עֹלַ֥ת שַׁבַּ֖ת בְּשַׁבַּתּ֑וֹ עַל־עֹלַ֥ת הַתָּמִ֖יד וְנִסְכָּֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: [the] burnt offering of sabbath in its sabbath, besides [the] burnt offering of the continuity and its drink offering.
pieces: as the burnt offering of each Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

L.10: the burnt offering of [every] sabbath on its sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.

R.10: This is the burnt offering for each Sabbath. Offer it in addition to the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering of sabbath on its sabbath: the offering for every Sabbath
decisions.reason: Repeating the word with "its" means each one in turn: the offering is brought on every Sabbath, week after week. Verse 14 says the same of the months.

decisions.choice: besides the continual burnt offering: added to the daily offering, not in place of it
decisions.reason: The word means "on top of". The Sabbath offering is brought as well as the two daily lambs, never instead of them. The same rule is repeated for each day in the calendar (verses 15, 23, 24, 31).

decisions.choice: [every]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "every" to show the sense of the repeated word. Balanced and Readable say "each Sabbath".

records.source: וּבְרָאשֵׁי֙ חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם תַּקְרִ֥יבוּ עֹלָ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה פָּרִ֨ים בְּנֵֽי־בָקָ֤ר שְׁנַ֨יִם֙ וְאַ֣יִל אֶחָ֔ד כְּבָשִׂ֧ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֛ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה תְּמִימִֽם׃
records.gloss: And at [the] beginnings of your months you will present [a] burnt offering to Yahweh: bulls, sons of [the] herd, two, and ram, one, lambs, sons of a year, seven, unblemished.
pieces: Each month, on its first day, you are to bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs in their first year, every one of them without defect.

L.11: And at the beginnings of your months you shall present a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: two bulls, young ones of the herd, and one ram, seven male lambs, sons of a year, unblemished.

R.11: When each new month begins, bring a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Bring two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old. None of them may have anything wrong with it.

decisions.choice: the beginnings of your months: the new moon, the first day of each month
decisions.reason: Israel's months followed the moon, and each began when the new moon first appeared. The day was marked with trumpets as well as offerings (10:10), and was a day of rest from trade in later times (Amos 8:5).

decisions.choice: two bulls, one ram, seven lambs: the larger set of festival offerings
decisions.reason: The new moon has the same burnt offerings as each day of Unleavened Bread (verse 19) and the day of firstfruits (verse 27): far more than the two lambs of the Sabbath. Seven lambs, the number of completeness, run through the festival lists.

decisions.choice: unblemished: all the animals, not the lambs only
decisions.reason: The word stands at the end of the list after the lambs, but it applies to every animal: all offerings had to be without defect (Leviticus 22:19-21), and verses 19 and 31 say so of the whole set.

decisions.choice: on its first day / when each new month begins
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the beginnings of your months". Balanced ("on its first day") and Readable ("when each new month begins") say what the phrase means, as at 10:10.

records.heading: Offerings at the start of each month

records.source: וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לַפָּ֖ר הָאֶחָ֑ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לָאַ֖יִל הָֽאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And three tenths [of] fine flour [as a] grain offering mixed with oil for the bull, the one, and two tenths [of] fine flour [as a] grain offering mixed with oil for the ram, the one,
pieces: The grain offering for each bull is to be {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil, and for the ram {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil,

L.12: And three tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil for each bull, and two tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil for the one ram,

R.12: For each bull, bring a grain offering of {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with olive oil. For the ram, bring a grain offering of {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with olive oil.

decisions.choice: three tenths for a bull, two tenths for a ram: more for a larger animal
decisions.reason: The grain offerings follow the scale of 15:4-9: for a bull three tenths of an ephah of flour, about six quarts; for a ram two tenths, about four quarts; for a lamb a tenth, about two quarts (verse 13).

decisions.choice: about 6 quarts; about 4 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Literal brackets "of an ephah", which the Hebrew leaves out.

records.source: וְעִשָּׂרֹ֣ן עִשָּׂר֗וֹן סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד עֹלָה֙ רֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and [a] tenth, [a] tenth [of] fine flour [as a] grain offering mixed with oil for the lamb, the one: [a] burnt offering, [an] aroma of soothing, [an] offering by fire to Yahweh.
pieces: and for each lamb {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering, a soothing aroma, a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: and a tenth [of an ephah], a tenth, of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil for each lamb: a burnt offering, an aroma of soothing, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: For each lamb, bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering. This burnt offering is a food offering burned on the altar, and its smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a tenth, a tenth: a tenth for each
decisions.reason: Saying the number twice means "so much each": every lamb has its own tenth of an ephah of flour. The same is said in verses 21 and 29.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering, an aroma of soothing: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The whole set, animals and grain together, is a gift the LORD gladly accepts.

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Literal shows the repeated "a tenth"; Balanced and Readable give its sense with "each".

records.source: וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֗ם חֲצִ֣י הַהִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַפָּ֜ר וּשְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַהִ֣ין לָאַ֗יִל וּרְבִיעִ֥ת הַהִ֛ין לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ יָ֑יִן זֹ֣את עֹלַ֥ת חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ בְּחָדְשׁ֔וֹ לְחָדְשֵׁ֖י הַשָּׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And their drink offerings, half of the hin will be for the bull, and [the] third of the hin for the ram, and [the] fourth of the hin for the lamb, [of] wine. This [is the] burnt offering of month in its month for [the] months of the year.
pieces: The wine for their drink offerings is to be {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} with each bull, {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} with the ram and {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} with each lamb. This is the burnt offering for the new moon, month after month through the year.

L.14: And their drink offerings shall be half of the hin for the bull, and a third of the hin for the ram, and a quarter of the hin for the lamb, of wine. This [is] the burnt offering of [each] month in its month, for the months of the year.

R.14: Also bring wine as a drink offering: {{units:about 2 quarts|half a hin}} for each bull, {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} for the ram, and {{units:about a quart|a quarter of a hin}} for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for the start of each month, all through the year.

decisions.choice: half, a third, a quarter of a hin: the wine for each animal
decisions.reason: The drink offerings follow the same scale as the grain: about two quarts of wine for a bull, about one and a quarter quarts for a ram, and about a quart for a lamb, as in 15:5-10.

decisions.choice: month in its month: each new moon in turn
decisions.reason: The word for "month" also means "new moon", the day that begins the month (verse 11). Said twice, with "its", it means every one in turn, as with the Sabbath in verse 10.

decisions.choice: of wine, named first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the wine only at the end of the list. Balanced and Readable name it with the first amount, so that the reader knows from the start what is measured.

records.source: וּשְׂעִ֨יר עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֛ד לְחַטָּ֖את לַיהוָ֑ה עַל־עֹלַ֧ת הַתָּמִ֛יד יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה וְנִסְכּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And [a] male goat of goats, one, for [a] sin offering to Yahweh; besides [the] burnt offering of the continuity it will be offered, and its drink offering.
pieces: Also one male goat is to be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

L.15: And one male goat of the goats for a sin offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; besides the continual burnt offering it shall be offered, and its drink offering.

R.15: Also offer one male goat to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a sin offering. Offer it in addition to the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

decisions.choice: sin offering: an offering that cleanses from sin and impurity
decisions.reason: The sin offering removed the stain of the people's sins and impurities from the sanctuary, so that the LORD could go on living among them (Leviticus 4; 16:16). From here on, every day of the festival calendar has one goat as a sin offering beside the burnt offerings (verses 22, 30). In these lists only here is the sin offering said in so many words to be "to the LORD".

decisions.choice: it shall be offered, and its drink offering: the goat is added to the daily offering
decisions.reason: "It" is the goat. "Its drink offering" belongs to the regular burnt offering, as in verse 10: the sin offering had no drink offering of its own.

decisions.choice: in addition to the regular burnt offering
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced says "in addition to" and Readable "daily burnt offering". Literal keeps "besides" and the Hebrew order, with the drink offering at the end.

records.source: וּבַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ פֶּ֖סַח לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And in the month the first, on [the] fourteenth day of the month, [is the] Passover to Yahweh.
pieces: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, the Passover is kept for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, [is] the Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: The Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is on the fourteenth day of the first month.

decisions.choice: the Passover: a household sacrifice, with no offerings for the whole people listed
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed and eaten by each household (Exodus 12:3-11; Numbers 9:1-14). So this list, which gives the offerings for the whole people, names its date only and gives no offerings for it.

decisions.choice: the first month: in the spring
decisions.reason: The year of festivals counts from the month of the exodus, in March or April (Exodus 12:2; Leviticus 23:5). The dates here are those of Leviticus 23:5-8.

records.heading: Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread

records.source: וּבַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר י֛וֹם לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֖ה חָ֑ג שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים מַצּ֖וֹת יֵאָכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And on [the] fifteenth day of the month the this [is a] festival; seven days unleavened bread will be eaten.
pieces: A festival is held on the fifteenth day of this month, and for seven days the bread eaten is to be made without yeast.

L.17: And on the fifteenth day of this month [is] a festival; seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.

R.17: On the fifteenth day of that month a festival begins. For seven days, the bread you eat must be made without yeast.

decisions.choice: festival: a feast kept at the sanctuary with rejoicing
decisions.reason: The word is used for the three yearly pilgrim festivals (Exodus 23:14-17). This one is not named here; it is the Festival of Unleavened Bread (Leviticus 23:6).

decisions.choice: unleavened bread: remembering the hurried departure from Egypt
decisions.reason: Unleavened bread is bread made without yeast. Israel ate it because they left Egypt in haste and their dough had no time to rise (Exodus 12:34, 39). The seven days run from the fifteenth to the twenty-first of the month (Exodus 12:18).

decisions.choice: bread made without yeast
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 23:6, Balanced and Readable say "bread made without yeast". Literal keeps "unleavened bread".

records.source: בַּיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן מִקְרָא־קֹ֑דֶשׁ כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: On the day the first [is a] convocation of holiness; any work of labor not you will do.
pieces: The first day is to be a holy assembly, when you do none of your ordinary work.

L.18: On the first day [there is] a holy convocation; any work of labor you shall not do.

R.18: On the first day, hold a holy gathering for worship. Do not do your everyday work.

decisions.choice: holy convocation: a sacred gathering called on a set day
decisions.reason: On such a day the people are called together for worship and ordinary work stops (Leviticus 23:2, 7).

decisions.choice: work of labor: ordinary daily work
decisions.reason: The phrase means the work of one's trade or livelihood. It is less than the "any work" of the Sabbath; food could be prepared on these days (Exodus 12:16; Leviticus 23:7).

decisions.choice: holy assembly / holy gathering for worship; ordinary work / everyday work
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 23:7. Literal keeps "holy convocation" and "work of labor".

records.source: וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֨ם אִשֶּׁ֤ה עֹלָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה פָּרִ֧ים בְּנֵי־בָקָ֛ר שְׁנַ֖יִם וְאַ֣יִל אֶחָ֑ד וְשִׁבְעָ֤ה כְבָשִׂים֙ בְּנֵ֣י שָׁנָ֔ה תְּמִימִ֖ם יִהְי֥וּ לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will present [an] offering by fire, [a] burnt offering to Yahweh: bulls, sons of [the] herd, two, and ram, one, and seven lambs, sons of a year; unblemished they will be for you.
pieces: You are to bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a food offering, a burnt offering made up of two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs in their first year. See that they are without defect.

L.19: And you shall present an offering by fire, a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: two bulls, young ones of the herd, and one ram, and seven male lambs, sons of a year; unblemished they shall be for you.

R.19: Bring a food offering to be burned on the altar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Offer as a burnt offering two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old. Make sure they have nothing wrong with them.

decisions.choice: the offerings of each day of Unleavened Bread: the same as at the new moon
decisions.reason: Leviticus 23:8 says that an offering by fire is brought each of the seven days, without giving the animals. They are given here: the same set as for the new moon (verse 11), every day of the festival (verse 24).

decisions.choice: unblemished they shall be for you: you must see to it that they are sound
decisions.reason: "For you" makes the people responsible for choosing animals without defect. It covers every animal in the list (Leviticus 22:19-21).

decisions.choice: See that they are / Make sure they have
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "they shall be for you" into a command to the people, which is its force.

records.source: וּמִ֨נְחָתָ֔ם סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשָּׁ֑מֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֜ים לַפָּ֗ר וּשְׁנֵ֧י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֛ים לָאַ֖יִל תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: And their grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram you will offer.
pieces: With them offer a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} for each bull and {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} for the ram.

L.20: And their grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths [of an ephah] for the bull and two tenths for the ram you shall offer.

R.20: With them bring a grain offering of fine flour mixed with olive oil. Bring {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} for each bull and {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} for the ram.

decisions.choice: three tenths, two tenths: as in verse 12
decisions.reason: The grain offerings are those of the new moon (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: about 6 quarts; about 4 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: עִשָּׂר֤וֹן עִשָּׂרוֹן֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד לְשִׁבְעַ֖ת הַכְּבָשִֽׂים׃
records.gloss: [A] tenth, [a] tenth you will offer for the lamb, the one, for [the] seven lambs.
pieces: For each of the seven lambs offer {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}}.

L.21: A tenth [of an ephah], a tenth, you shall offer for each lamb, for the seven lambs.

R.21: Bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} for each of the seven lambs.

decisions.choice: a tenth, a tenth: a tenth for each lamb
decisions.reason: As in verse 13. The verb is singular here, speaking to Israel as one, as in verse 4.

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts (units setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

records.source: וּשְׂעִ֥יר חַטָּ֖את אֶחָ֑ד לְכַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] male goat [of] sin offering, one, to make atonement for you.
pieces: Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

L.22: And one male goat [as] a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

R.22: Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for you: to remove the people's sin so that they can stay near God
decisions.reason: To make atonement is to wipe away sin and impurity by the offering God has given, so that the people are forgiven and the LORD can go on living among them (Leviticus 4:20; 16:30). "You" is plural, the whole people. For the sin offering see verse 15.

decisions.choice: a male goat: the list goes on without a verb
decisions.reason: The verse adds the goat to the burnt offerings of verse 19, with no verb of its own.

decisions.choice: Also offer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "Also offer", since in English the verse needs a verb. Literal brackets "as" and keeps the bare list.

records.source: מִלְּבַד֙ עֹלַ֣ת הַבֹּ֔קֶר אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְעֹלַ֣ת הַתָּמִ֑יד תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־אֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: Besides [the] burnt offering of the morning which [is] for [the] burnt offering of the continuity you will offer these.
pieces: All this is to be offered besides the morning burnt offering, which belongs to the regular burnt offering.

L.23: Besides the burnt offering of the morning, which [is] for the continual burnt offering, you shall offer these.

R.23: Offer all these as well as the morning lamb of the daily burnt offering.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering of the morning, which is for the continual burnt offering: the morning lamb of the daily offering
decisions.reason: "The burnt offering of the morning" is the morning lamb of verse 4, part of the daily offering. The festival offerings are brought as well as this, not in place of it. Only the morning lamb is named, perhaps because the festival offerings were brought after it on the same morning; the evening lamb is still offered (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the morning lamb of the daily burnt offering
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two names of the offering into one phrase, so that the reader sees that the morning offering is part of the daily one, and names the lamb of verse 4.

records.source: כָּאֵ֜לֶּה תַּעֲשׂ֤וּ לַיּוֹם֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים לֶ֛חֶם אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה עַל־עוֹלַ֧ת הַתָּמִ֛יד יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה וְנִסְכּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Like these you will offer for the day seven days, food of [an] offering by fire, [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh; besides [the] burnt offering of the continuity it will be offered, and its drink offering.
pieces: Offer this food each day for seven days as a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is added to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

L.24: Like these you shall offer daily for seven days, food of an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; besides the continual burnt offering it shall be offered, and its drink offering.

R.24: Bring the same offerings every day for seven days. They are food for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, food offerings burned on the altar, and their smell pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Offer them in addition to the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.

decisions.choice: like these daily for seven days: the same offerings each day of the festival
decisions.reason: Each of the seven days of Unleavened Bread has the full set of verses 19-22: two bulls, a ram, seven lambs and a goat. At the Festival of Booths the number of bulls goes down day by day (29:12-34); here it stays the same.

decisions.choice: food of an offering by fire: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The offerings are again called the LORD's food, gifts set before him (verse 2).

decisions.choice: their smell pleases him
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD once and then uses "him" for him, to keep the sentence short.

records.source: וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִקְרָא־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשֽׂוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And on the day the seventh [a] convocation of holiness will be for you; any work of labor not you will do.
pieces: The seventh day is to be a holy assembly for you, when you do none of your ordinary work.

L.25: And on the seventh day a holy convocation shall be for you; any work of labor you shall not do.

R.25: On the seventh day, hold another holy gathering for worship. Do not do your everyday work.

decisions.choice: the seventh day: the festival ends as it began
decisions.reason: The first and last days of the festival are holy days of rest from ordinary work (verse 18; Leviticus 23:7-8).

decisions.choice: another
decisions.reason: Readable adds "another" to link this day to the first day of verse 18, as in Leviticus 23:8. For the other wording see verse 18.

records.source: וּבְי֣וֹם הַבִּכּוּרִ֗ים בְּהַקְרִ֨יבְכֶ֜ם מִנְחָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּשָׁבֻעֹ֖תֵיכֶ֑ם מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: And on [the] day of the firstfruits, when you present [a] grain offering new to Yahweh at your weeks, [a] convocation of holiness will be for you; any work of labor not you will do.
pieces: The day of firstfruits, when you bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a grain offering from the new crop at your Festival of Weeks, is to be a holy assembly for you. Do none of your ordinary work.

L.26: And on the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new grain offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at your [festival of] weeks, a holy convocation shall be for you; any work of labor you shall not do.

R.26: The day of firstfruits comes at your Festival of Weeks. On that day, when you bring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a grain offering from the new harvest, hold a holy gathering for worship. Do not do your everyday work.

decisions.choice: the day of the firstfruits: the festival of the first wheat
decisions.reason: "Firstfruits" are the first produce to ripen (Leviticus 2:14; Numbers 18:13). This day is the festival at the end of the grain harvest, when the first bread from the new wheat was brought (Leviticus 23:15-21; Exodus 34:22).

decisions.choice: at your weeks: at the Festival of Weeks
decisions.reason: "Weeks" stands for the festival named after the seven weeks counted from the first sheaf of the barley harvest (Leviticus 23:15-16; Deuteronomy 16:9-10). It is kept on the fiftieth day.

decisions.choice: a new grain offering: an offering from the harvest just gathered
decisions.reason: "New" means from the new crop, the two loaves of Leviticus 23:16-17. For the holy convocation and the work of labor see verse 18.

decisions.choice: Festival of Weeks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "your weeks". Balanced and Readable say "Festival of Weeks"; Literal brackets "festival of". Balanced and Readable say "from the new crop" or "new harvest" for "new", as in Leviticus 23:16.

records.heading: The day of firstfruits

records.source: וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֨ם עוֹלָ֜ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה פָּרִ֧ים בְּנֵי־בָקָ֛ר שְׁנַ֖יִם אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֑ד שִׁבְעָ֥ה כְבָשִׂ֖ים בְּנֵ֥י שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will present [a] burnt offering for [an] aroma of soothing to Yahweh: bulls, sons of [the] herd, two, ram, one, seven lambs, sons of a year,
pieces: You are to present a burnt offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, of two young bulls, one ram and seven year-old male lambs,

L.27: And you shall present a burnt offering for an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: two bulls, young ones of the herd, one ram, seven male lambs, sons of a year,

R.27: Bring a burnt offering whose smell pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old.

decisions.choice: two bulls, one ram, seven lambs: not the same as the list in Leviticus 23:18
alternatives: two accounts of one set of offerings
decisions.reason: Here the day of firstfruits has the same burnt offerings as the new moon and Unleavened Bread (verses 11, 19). Leviticus 23:18, describing the same day, lists seven lambs, one bull and two rams to be offered with the new bread. The text does not say how the two lists relate. They may be two sets of offerings brought on the same day, one for the festival and one with the loaves, or two accounts of one set.

records.source: וּמִנְחָתָ֔ם סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשָּׁ֑מֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶשְׂרֹנִים֙ לַפָּ֣ר הָֽאֶחָ֔ד שְׁנֵי֙ עֶשְׂרֹנִ֔ים לָאַ֖יִל הָאֶחָֽד׃

decisions.choice: about 6 quarts; about 4 quarts (units setting)

decisions.choice: a tenth, a tenth: a tenth for each lamb

records.source: שְׂעִ֥יר עִזִּ֖ים אֶחָ֑ד לְכַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: [a] male goat of goats, one, to make atonement for you.
pieces: and one male goat to make atonement for you.

L.30: one male goat of the goats, to make atonement for you.

R.30: Also offer one male goat to make atonement for you.

decisions.choice: a male goat to make atonement: the sin offering of verse 22
decisions.reason: The words "sin offering" are not repeated here, but the goat offered to make atonement is the sin offering of the festival, as in verses 15 and 22.

decisions.choice: Also offer
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the verb, as in verse 22. Literal and Balanced end the list of verses 27-30 with this verse.

records.source: מִלְּבַ֞ד עֹלַ֧ת הַתָּמִ֛יד וּמִנְחָת֖וֹ תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיוּ־לָכֶ֖ם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: Besides [the] burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering you will offer; unblemished they will be for you; and their drink offerings.
pieces: Bring all these besides the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings with them. The animals must be without defect.

L.31: Besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering you shall offer [them]; unblemished they shall be for you; and their drink offerings.

R.31: Bring these animals and their drink offerings as well as the daily burnt offering and its grain offering. None of the animals may have anything wrong with it.

decisions.choice: and their drink offerings: the drink offerings of the festival animals
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "and their drink offerings" at the end, after the words about the animals being without defect. "Their" means the bulls, ram and lambs of verse 27, whose wine is to be brought with them in the amounts of verse 14.

decisions.choice: unblemished they shall be for you: as in verse 19
decisions.reason: The people are to see that every animal is without defect. The words cover all the animals of verses 27-30.

decisions.choice: its grain offering: the grain offering of the daily lambs
decisions.reason: Here the daily offering is named with its grain offering (verse 5), where verses 10, 15 and 24 name its drink offering. Both go with it.

decisions.choice: their drink offerings with them / these animals and their drink offerings
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "with them" so that the drink offerings are joined to the festival animals; Readable moves them next to "these animals". Both put the words about defects last and say "the animals" for "they".
